title: Soft-reserve token bucket for dedicated capacity with retroactive SLA recredit automation
creator: Leah Kim
description: Background: Customers on Dedicated capacity occasionally observe transient throttles during short-lived hot-traffic bursts even though their monthly reserved throughput is sufficient. Current burst handling is either strict (hard throttle) or permissive but unaccounted (best-effort). Proposal: implement a per-tenant "soft-reserve" token bucket that allows short bursts above reserved throughput using time-decaying soft tokens, paired with an automated retroactive SLA recredit pipeline that computes and issues billing credits when the platform fails to satisfy reserved throughput guarantees.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Soft-reserve tokens are minted and consumed per-tenant; enforcement lives at the serving gateway with <3ms p95 added latency for request path
2) Default soft-token burst capacity equals 25% of tenant reserved throughput or configurable override (whichever lower), with token decay half-life of 10 minutes; configurable by runtime flag
3) Automated SLA recredit job identifies under-served tenant-minute windows and posts compensating ledger credits; end-to-end crediting latency (detection -> ledger entry) <24 hours
4) No regressions in existing billing reconciliation pipelines; unit tests + integration tests for event-sourced ledger flows are present and green
5) Telemetry exposes per-tenant minted/consumed tokens, leftover token distribution, and per-tenant shortfall in tokens for the past 30 days in Console dashboards
technical_notes: Design summary: soft-reserve tokens live in a per-tenant lightweight counter (in-memory sharded cache) backed by event-sourced persistent store for eventual reconciliation. Tokens are minted when a tenant's reserved headroom is underutilized for a sliding window; tokens decay deterministically to avoid unbounded accumulation.

Token lifecycle: Mint -> Hold -> Consume -> Decay. Minting rule: every 1s of unused reserved throughput yields tokens proportional to (reserved - observedutil) clipped to 25% cap. Token TTL: 60 minutes with exponential decay (half-life 10m).

Enforcement: Gateway checks current tokens before allowing burst above reserved throughput and emits X-Soft-Token-Used header for tracing. If tokens exhausted, fallback to existing throttling policy (leaky bucket/hard throttle depending on pool config).

Metering/ledger integration: consumption events emit metering-event.v1 to stream (Kafka); accounting service aggregates per-minute consumption vs reserved and records offsets to billing-ledger as adjustment claims. The recredit pipeline consumes the same topic and runs a deterministic job to calculate SLA shortfall using request timestamps and pool capacity snapshots.
Implementation components: metering-service (mint/emit), gateway-enforcer, token-cache (redis/embedded), compensator-worker (job), ledger-service API, observability hooks (metrics + tracing).

Data model sketch: ledger entries created by compensator-worker use type="sla_recredit", reason="soft-reserve-shortfall", reference_window=YYYYMMDDTHHMM, amount_units=integer_tokens_or_cost. Entries include original capacity-snapshot-id for audit. (Represented here as strings only).

Performance trade-offs: keeping token state purely in redis offers low latency but risks state staleness on failover. We'll use an append-only event log to reconstruct cache on restart and rely on conservative reinflation to avoid over-crediting.
rollout_plan: 1) Spike/prototype: implement token minting simulator and offline recredit job on staging (2 weeks)
2) Canary: enable soft-reserve enforcement for internal tenants + 5 pilot customers with telemetry-only mode for 1 week
3) Controlled enable: soft-enforce for 10% of eligible dedicated pools with compensator-worker in dry-run (no ledger writes) for 48 hours
4) Full enforcement + enabling recredit job in write-mode behind feature flag; monitor for invoice drift and run manual verifications
5) GA: enable for all Dedicated pools with ability to opt-out per-tenant in Console
monitoring: Metrics to add: tenant.soft_token.minted.count, tenant.soft_token.consumed.count, tenant.soft_token.available.gauge, tenant.sla_shortfall.tokens.count
Dashboards: per-tenant 24h view of mint/consume/shortfall; heatmap for pools showing token exhaustion events
Alerts: >0.5% of total reserved throughput consumed from soft-tokens for more than 5 consecutive minutes in a pool (investigate misconfiguration), compensator-job failure rate >1% (P0)
Audit logs: ledger entries tagged with compensator-job-run-id and service-commit sha for forensics
deployment_considerations: All changes behind runtime feature flags and tenant opt-outs; default to disabled for existing tenants until pilots complete
Data residency: token cache data does not contain PII; ledger adjustments must follow KMS-signed requests and audit trails consistent with Private deployments
Backwards compatibility: metering event schema adds optional fields (soft_token_{minted,consumed}) that consumers must tolerate missing fields
DB migrations: append-only event table (metering_events_v2) - no destructive migration planned
risks_and_mitigations: Over-crediting risk: compensator job uses conservative shortfall calculation (floor) and an independent reconciliation job will run nightly to detect anomalous credits; manual rollback path exists
State loss on region failover: use event-sourced reconstruction with conservative reinflation to prevent granting more tokens than earned
Billing complexity: communicate feature to finance and support with clear docs and sample invoice lines; ensure invoice delta for pilots reviewed before GA
Latency regressions: keep gateway check path minimal; if instrumentation shows >3ms p95 added, revert enforcement and continue in telemetry-only mode
comments: 2026-02-26 Leah Kim: Spike completed. Prototype minted tokens in offline sim and validated decay curve. Observed median token availability under 10% for bursty tenants.
2026-03-02 Marco Santos: Design review notes - prefer Redis streams for short-term cache replication; compensator-worker should be idempotent keyed by (tenant,window) to avoid double credits.

2026-03-05 Priya Patel (Billing): Confirmed ledger schema acceptable. Request: add amount_in_currency string for human-readable invoice line. Also asked for a nightly audit CSV export for finance vetting.

2026-03-09 Nikhil Rao (SRE): Suggest adding canary throttle rules per-AZ to avoid cross-AZ token bleed during AZ-level resource shifts. Also raised concern about compensator job DBA locks under high cardinality — we'll shard job by tenant-hash.
2026-03-12 Design review: UX mockups attached for Console opt-out and per-tenant soft-reserve slider (max 25%). Action: DES-210 to design final copy and help text.

2026-03-14 Marco Santos: Implementation plan drafted. Opening branches: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6872 (metering-service), https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/2910 (gateway-enforcer).
notes_for_support: Support playbook: explain soft-reserve behavior, show Console opt-out, provide ledger entry id for any recredit. If customer disputes crediting, follow finance CSV and compensator-job-run-id to audit.
final_decision: Defer to telemetry-only for first 2 pilot weeks; compensator-worker in dry-run mode during telemetry-only. After sign-off from billing and SRE, enable write-mode.
